clue.text: Repellent poisoner spiking drink, source of beer in it

indicators.note: spiking a drink means slipping something into it, so the poisoner goes inside the drink

parts.note: hock is a German white wine

indicators.note: to repel is to drive back, so the poisoner's name is sent backwards

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, a natural poisoner

explanation.surface: A nasty poisoner doctors someone's drink, with a hint of beer in the glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repellent' sends the snake backwards, giving PSA, and 'spiking' slips that into the wine. Hock is a British name for German white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack of this kind is the bag that holds the hops brewers use, so beer's source is in it.

clue.text: Coppers, obsolete money?

parts.note: something obsolete is old, out of date
a bill is a banknote, paper money

explanation.surface: Is a policeman worth only antiquated cash?
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppers are police officers, and British slang names the police collectively this way.

clue.text: Designated partners primarily desperate for a quickie potential romance?

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild, frantic disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement
primarily points to the first letter of the word partners

explanation.surface: Matched couples, keen and desperate, hurry towards a possible fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' rearranges DESIGNATED plus P, the first letter of 'partners' signalled by 'primarily'.
explanation.definitionFit: At these events singles meet many prospective partners in quick few-minute chats, a fast route to possible romance.

clue.text: Line that's curved up around mouth, say — there's disease

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps round the second
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
a mouth is an example of a hole, an opening; say marks the example

explanation.surface: A curled-up lip around someone's mouth is a sign of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the curve, giving CRA, which wraps 'around' the opening.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an acute bacterial infection of the intestine, spread by contaminated water.

clue.text: Cold peaks, flipping ___ cold one

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole run over, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: the gap printed in the clue is literally a blank space
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker curses some cold mountain tops.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank in the clue is itself a piece: SPACE. 'flipping' reverses SPACE + C + I as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar caps of ice cover high, frozen peaks and summits, so they are cold tops.

clue.text: See 21
Sea creature with black, spotless raised scale

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: spotless means pure, unblemished

explanation.surface: A shellfish with dark, clean, lifted scales.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall is to climb it with effort, using hands and feet.

clue.text: US city where chicken eating duck seen in photos

indicators.note: seen in means the next pieces sit inside the word for photos

parts.note: pix is informal for pictures, photos

indicators.note: eating means the bird swallows, so contains, the duck

parts.note: a hen is a chicken
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A snapshot of an American town shows a hen gulping a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the state capital of Arizona, a major American urban centre.

clue.text: Both man and woman married — hope this is not confusing!

indicators.note: confusing jumbles things, so the letters are mixed into a new order
is not means the letters of the word is are taken away from this

explanation.surface: Someone who has wed hopes the arrangement does not baffle anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: THIS without IS ('is not') leaves TH; 'confusing' rearranges MARRIED + HOPE + TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a creature has both male and female sexual organs, combining the two sexes.

clue.text: Advantage in landed gentry

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words landed gentry

explanation.surface: The privileged landowning class has a head start.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand or a slight lead over rivals is a competitive margin.

clue.text: Pa wants nose doubly reshaped? Time for much criticism

indicators.note: reshaped means the letters are given a new form, rearranged
doubly means the word nose is used twice

explanation.surface: Father wants a nose job done twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' takes NOSE twice; 'reshaped' rearranges PA + NOSE + NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a period when someone may be attacked by all, from hunting seasons.

clue.text: Played trick?

definitions.meaning: a violin, an instrument that is played

explanation.walkthrough: A definition and a half: the question mark lets 'Played' stand as an adjective for the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin is the bowed instrument people play, and as a verb the word means to cheat or swindle.

clue.text: Grind put ahead of financial reserve, territory abandoned by Labour

indicators.note: put ahead of places the first piece before the second

parts.note: a mill grinds corn
a bank is a reserve or store of money

explanation.surface: Grinding comes before saving money, in a seat Labour left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Millbank, by the Thames in London, housed the Labour Party's headquarters until it moved out.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street held Labour's famous campaign headquarters, a base the party later vacated.

clue.text: What six outraged dwarves might do, being reckless?

definitions.text: What six outraged dwarves might do
definitions.meaning: if one of the seven dwarves in the Snow White story, Happy, annoyed the other six, they might strike him

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a careless, cheerfully irresponsible or punch-drunk attitude.

clue.text: Flower on male cobblers

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a poppy is a flower
a cock is a male bird

explanation.surface: A bloom is pinned to the man who mends shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' is British slang for nonsense, not shoemakers here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British terms for nonsense or rubbish talk.

clue.text: Agent, beast punching nose

indicators.note: punching means one piece is driven into the other

parts.note: to nose is to pry, poke about
an ox is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: An animal thumps someone on the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy or agent acts on someone's behalf, for instance casting a vote for them.

clue.text: Boy flipped over full of pee-pee, say, and residue — painful result?

indicators.note: full of means the name contains the next piece
flipped over means the boy's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Ryan is a boy's name

indicators.note: say tells us the two words are spoken as letters

parts.note: pee-pee said out loud is the letters P P
ash is what is left after burning

explanation.surface: A baby boy, turned over, full of wee and leftovers, ends up sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped over' gives NAYR, and 'full of' puts the two letters inside it. 'Nappy' is the British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A red, sore skin irritation is a painful consequence of wet nappies for infants.

clue.text: No end in sight, fatal passing around a river in desert

indicators.note: passing around means the trimmed word goes round the next pieces
with no end in sight, the first and last letters of fatal are dropped

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A deadly trek around a river in the desert seems endless.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'sight' in the clue does no work beyond the surface: 'No end' trims both ends of fatal, and the result goes 'passing around' the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This arid plateau in northern Chile is one of the driest places on Earth.

clue.text: Expression of concern about despairing gasp, but they're not yet croaking!

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a frown is a worried look

indicators.note: despairing suggests being in a state, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A worried face greets a desperate gasp, though no one is dying yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'despairing' rearranges GASP into GSPA, which FROWN goes 'about'. 'Croaking' looks like dying; it is the frogs' call.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs laid by frogs have not yet hatched into creatures able to croak.

clue.text: Dizzy on a horse? Let's go faster!

parts.note: giddy means dizzy
a rider on a horse is up

explanation.surface: A dazed rider in the saddle urges more speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders call this to urge a horse onward, an exclamation meaning hurry up.

clue.text: Two Barbaras making a pile for Elizabeth?

parts.note: Barbara Windsor was a British actress famed for Carry On films
Barbara Castle was a British Labour cabinet minister

explanation.surface: A pair of women named Barbara build a stately home for a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: A pile is a grand building.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal residence in Berkshire is a great stately building used by the Queen.

clue.text: Ape, head like an elephant, climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the run is read upward, backwards

parts.note: nob is slang for head
an elephant is big

explanation.surface: A primate with an elephant-shaped head goes up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-armed tree-dwelling primate of south-east Asia is a lesser ape.

clue.text: One's spotted women, genteel and otherwise

parts.note: lady is the genteel word for a woman
bird is the slang, less refined word for a woman

explanation.surface: Polite ladies and others are all being noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: This small red beetle has black spots on its wing cases.

clue.text: See 3
Cards bitter-sweet, including The Circle

indicators.note: including means the word for bitter holds the circle

parts.note: tart means sharp or bitter, and a tart is also a sweet pastry
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A bittersweet pack of cards includes one called The Circle.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a special deck of cards used for fortune-telling.

clue.text: Party behind horse sandwiches — more traditional filling supplied here?

indicators.note: sandwiches means the horse goes either side of the other pieces

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
Con is short for the Conservative party
butt is slang for backside, behind

explanation.surface: A party follows a horse and serves sandwiches with old-fashioned fillings.
explanation.walkthrough: A butty is a British word for a sandwich; this one is filled with bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: This British sandwich holds a classic filling of fried rashers, the traditional choice.

clue.text: See 17
Main problem hiding the family's excruciatingly embarrassing habit?

indicators.note: hiding means the next piece is concealed inside
problem signals the letters are in trouble, so rearranged

parts.note: kin are one's family

explanation.surface: The chief problem conceals a family's awkward routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges the first word into MANI, which 'hiding' wraps round the family. Habit here means clothing, as in a riding habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's skimpy one-piece swimsuit is a garment, a habit, infamous for embarrassment.

clue.text: Arrogant type puts manoeuvring before skill

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next
manoeuvring moves things around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: art is skill

explanation.surface: A pushy person rates scheming above talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A presumptuous newcomer who has risen fast and acts self-important.
